Salt Lake County by the numbers

What is Salt Lake County, Utah, and how is it laid out?

Salt Lake County is Utah's most populous county and holds the state capital, Salt Lake City, as its county seat. The county was organized on January 31, 1850, and the 2020 census counted 1,185,238 residents, with a 2025 estimate of 1,220,916.

It covers 807 square miles, of which 742 are land, and it fills the Salt Lake Valley between the Wasatch Range on the east and the Oquirrh Mountains on the west. The Jordan River runs north through the valley and the Great Salt Lake borders the northwest corner.

Cities in the county include West Valley City, West Jordan, South Jordan, Sandy, Murray, Draper, Herriman, Riverton, Midvale, Taylorsville, Holladay, Millcreek, Cottonwood Heights, Bluffdale and South Salt Lake, along with unincorporated Magna, Kearns and Copperton. Each of these sits in the same county tax system, so the dates and offices below apply across them.

What shapes the Salt Lake County economy?

The county's gross domestic product reached $153.846 billion in 2024, and its economy has long mixed services, mining, defense and health care. The Bingham Canyon Mine is among the largest open-pit mines in the world, Northrop Grumman builds solid rocket motors in Magna, and the University of Utah, Intermountain Health Care and University of Utah Healthcare are among the biggest employers.

Winter sports have mattered since Alta Ski Area opened in 1939. Salt Lake City International Airport is a hub for Delta and SkyWest, TRAX light rail runs three lines, and FrontRunner commuter rail links Ogden to Provo. Interstates 15, 80 and 215 cross the valley. For a seller, proximity to rail and the freeway grid is a usable talking point.

What does the Salt Lake County climate and geology mean for a home?

The valley is dry, averaging about 15 inches of precipitation a year, but it gets roughly 55 inches of snow, and winter temperature inversions trap pollution on the valley floor. Heavier snow falls on the benches, up to about 100 inches.

The Wasatch Fault runs along the mountain front. It is about 240 miles long, roughly 80% of Utah's people live along it, and one source gives a 57% chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger earthquake within 50 years. Buyers and inspectors may ask about it. If your house has had foundation repair, a chimney fix or a retrofit, keep the paperwork in one folder.

Which Salt Lake County offices handle what?

Several county offices touch a property sale. The Assessor appraises property as of January 1 and completes the assessment roll by May 22, and the Auditor mails Notices of Valuation and Tax Change around July 22. The offices below handle billing, recording and appeals.

OfficeWhat it doesContact
TreasurerBills and collects tax, runs tax relief2001 S State St, Suite N1-200; 385-468-8300; treasurer@saltlakecounty.gov
RecorderRecords deeds and other documents2001 S State St, Suite N1-600; 385-468-8145
Board of EqualizationHears value appeals2002 S State St, #N3-300; PO Box 144575

The Treasurer's office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and its tax relief division answers at 385-468-8300, option 2.

What are the key Salt Lake County property tax dates?

The main deadline is November 30, the last day to pay the current year's property tax without a penalty. If it falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. Official tax notices must be mailed by November 1.

  • January 1: the Assessor appraises property and establishes ownership.
  • Around July 22: valuation notices go out.
  • August 1: the appeal window at the Board of Equalization opens.
  • September 15: the appeal window closes, or 45 days after the notice, whichever is later.
  • December 1: unpaid tax becomes delinquent.
  • January 31: the penalty rises if the balance is still unpaid.

The delinquency penalty on December 1 is the greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel. It drops to the greater of 1% or $10 if you pay in full by January 31. After that, the penalty returns to 2.5% plus interest retroactive to January 1. A seller who closes in December or January should ask the title company whether the bill is paid.

How does the residential exemption work when a house changes hands?

Utah taxes a qualifying primary home on 55% of its market value because of a 45% residential exemption. The Utah State Tax Commission says the home must be occupied as a primary domicile for at least 183 consecutive days in a calendar year, by the owner or a full-time tenant, and a household may claim only one.

The exemption does not move to a new owner automatically. The buyer files a new declaration, which Form TC-473A covers starting January 1, 2027, and the application is due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. A late or missing filing can leave the house taxed at 100% of market value for that year. If you are selling, tell your buyer about this step.

How do you appeal a Salt Lake County valuation?

You appeal to the county Board of Equalization, and the 2026 deadline is September 15. In-person filings must arrive by 5:00 p.m. that day, mailed filings must be postmarked by then, and online filings must be finished by 11:59 p.m.

  • Email the signed application and all evidence to propertytaxappeals@saltlakecounty.gov, or mail it to the Board at 2002 S State St #N3-300.
  • Useful evidence includes at least three recent comparable sales, a professional appraisal, documented errors in county records, and your own purchase documents.
  • If you bought between July 1 of the prior year and June 30 of the current year, the closing statement is often strong evidence.

Independent hearing officers review the evidence and recommend a decision, and the Board decides whether the value goes up, goes down or stays. The county says to pay the bill by the due date even if the appeal is pending, because refunds come only after a final decision. A county Board decision can be appealed to the State Tax Commission within 30 days.

What tax relief programs does the Salt Lake County Treasurer offer?

The Treasurer runs several relief programs for owners who meet age, income or status rules. Applications open January 1, and the statutory deadline is September 1.

ProgramWho qualifies
Circuit BreakerAge 67 or older, or a surviving spouse, with household income up to $44,221
Indigent ReliefAge 65 or older or receiving disability benefits, with income and assets below $44,221
Senior DeferralHomeowners age 75 or older meeting income and asset rules
Veteran ReliefVeterans with a service-related disability, or out-of-state active duty members
Blind ReliefLegally blind owners and certain survivors
Hardship ReliefExtreme hardship, subject to income and asset limits

A deferral or relief claim on a house you plan to sell affects the payoff figure, so ask the Treasurer about it early.

What happens if Salt Lake County property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid tax can end in a tax sale after about five years. The redemption period expires on March 15 of the fifth year after the taxes become delinquent, and the Auditor holds the final sale on the fourth Thursday of May. Owners can still pay up until the sale.

Notice runs in a newspaper for four weeks and is mailed to owners and interested parties. Ask the Treasurer for an exact payoff figure if you are in this position. A sale that closes before the redemption deadline lets escrow pay the balance out of the proceeds.

What does it take to record a deed in Salt Lake County?

The Salt Lake County Recorder charges a flat $40 per recording, and the document must meet formatting and notary rules. The Recorder's office is at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, and it is open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

  • White 8.5 by 11 inch paper, printed on one side, with black text.
  • A 2.5 by 4.5 inch blank space in the upper right corner of the first page.
  • The parcel serial number, a legal description for property in the county, and the grantee's address.
  • An original signature with a notary acknowledgment and a legible stamp.

Title companies handle this, but a deed signed outside a closing, such as one between family members, needs the same care.

More questions about Salt Lake County, UT Property Tax Guide

When are Salt Lake County property taxes due?

November 30 is the last day to pay the current year's tax without penalty. If that date lands on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day. Unpaid tax becomes delinquent on December 1.

What is the deadline to appeal a Salt Lake County property value?

The deadline is September 15, or 45 days after the valuation notice is mailed, whichever is later. For 2026, the county set September 15 as the filing deadline. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization.

Does the Utah residential exemption transfer to the buyer?

No. The exemption does not transfer automatically, and the buyer must file a new declaration. A late or missing filing can mean taxation at 100% of market value for that year.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Salt Lake County?

The flat recording fee is $40 per recording, with $2 more for each legal description over 10. A recorded copy costs $2 per page.

What happens to a Salt Lake County house after the redemption period?

The redemption period ends March 15 of the fifth year after the tax becomes delinquent, and the Auditor holds the tax sale in late May. You can still pay the balance until the sale takes place.

Can I get property tax relief as a senior in Salt Lake County?

Possibly. The Treasurer lists Circuit Breaker relief for ages 67 and up with income up to $44,221 and a Senior Deferral for owners 75 and older. Call 385-468-8300, option 2, to check eligibility.
